before:
Weighbridge Terminal — Queue Assignment Settings

The terminal software calls waiting vehicles from a single holding yard, and the duty operator fixes the calling order at the start of each shift. As configured for the autumn beet season, livestock loads are called ahead of aggregate loads, and aggregate loads ahead of general haulage. Every class of vehicle remains entitled to a weighing slot on the day it presents, and no load may be turned away for want of a slot; the setting governs only the sequence in which the yard is emptied. Operators are asked not to alter the setting part way through a shift, since drivers are given an estimated calling time on arrival and several complaints have followed from those times moving backwards.

before:
Fen Drainage Board — Sluice Handover at Shift Change

Handover between keepers takes place at the sluice house, not by telephone, and the incoming keeper walks the penstock deck before signing. The outgoing keeper may leave the penstock partly raised overnight, provided the tell-tale float is set to the low mark. Gauge boards are read together and both readings entered in the day book, with any disagreement of more than fifty millimetres referred to the district officer before either keeper leaves the site. Keys to the winch cabin pass hand to hand; they are not left in the meter box. The board reviews handover practice after each period of prolonged rainfall and circulates any amendments to all four stations.
after:
Fen Drainage Board — Sluice Handover at Shift Change

Handover between keepers takes place at the sluice house, not by telephone, and the incoming keeper walks the penstock deck before signing. The outgoing keeper must lower the penstock fully before leaving, whatever mark the tell-tale float has been set to. Gauge boards are read together and both readings entered in the day book, with any disagreement of more than fifty millimetres referred to the district officer before either keeper leaves the site. Keys to the winch cabin pass hand to hand; they are not left in the meter box. The board reviews handover practice after each period of prolonged rainfall and circulates any amendments to all four stations.
variation_site: The change falls in the second sentence of the paragraph.
author_note: Turns a permission into a requirement; the steps and the readings are untouched.

before:
Estuary Ringing Group — Recorder's Correspondence Register

The register lists every report of a ringed bird received from the public, with the finder's address and the date of acknowledgement. Acknowledgements go out on the standard slip, which reads: Dear Sir or Madam, the Group acknowledges with thanks your report of a ringed bird and will write again once the ringing details have been traced. Where a bird was ringed abroad the slip is held back until the foreign scheme replies, and the delay is noted in the final column. Slips are signed by the recorder and copied to the county archive at the end of each season, unless the finder has asked to remain unnamed.

before:
Tide Gauge Manual — Section 4, Well Siltation

The stilling well takes water through a single inlet pipe set below the lowest astronomical tide, and fine material settles there over the year. Comparison against the staff gauge suggests that the well may silt at roughly four millimetres a year, though the evidence rests on two seasons of readings from one station. Keepers should clear the inlet each spring and record the date on the maintenance card. Where the difference between float and staff exceeds ten millimetres before the spring clearance, the station is to be reported to the regional office, which will arrange an out-of-season visit and, if required, a diver's inspection of the inlet mouth.
after:
Tide Gauge Manual — Section 4, Well Siltation

author_note: Hard: the hedging is dropped while the four-millimetre figure and every instruction stay exactly as they were, tempting a reading as a changed observation.

before:
Ternery Warden's Bulletin — June Count

Wardens walked the shingle spit at low water on the fourth and fifth of June, working outward from the eastern marker post as in previous years. The count recorded 212 occupied nests, with the densest cluster north of the old cable run. Fencing held through the spring gales and no dog incursions were logged. Two nests were lost to tidal wash on the seaward edge and have been marked on the sketch map for next year's fence line. Volunteers are reminded that the spit is closed to walkers until the fifteenth of August and that the loudhailer is kept in the shed by the slipway.

before:
Quarry Haul Road — Notice to Drivers: Detaching Trailers

This notice applies in the lower stocking yard only, where the standing is on compacted fines and the fall is towards the settling pond. On arriving at the marked bay, chock the trailer wheels, then wind down the landing legs, then disconnect the air lines and release the coupling. Do not detach on the ramp under any circumstance. High-visibility clothing is worn throughout and the yard shunter must be told before any unit moves off. Drivers who cannot complete the detachment unaided are to wait for the shunter rather than seek help from loader operators, who cannot leave their machines while the crusher is running.

before:
Harbour Office Handbook — Mooring Charges, West Basin

Berth holders are invoiced in March for the twelve months following, and part years are charged in whole months. Annual mooring charges are worked out from the 1998 sliding-scale table, entered at the vessel's registered overall length. Tenders under three metres carried on davits are not charged separately. Late payment attracts the standing surcharge after twenty-eight days, and a berth may be reallocated once an invoice is ninety days outstanding. Holders wintering ashore in the boatyard remain liable for the water frontage element. Queries go to the harbour clerk in writing; the duty staff on the pontoon gate cannot vary an invoice.

before:

One line is written for every passage and one at each reading of the upstream gauge, in the bound book kept in the cabin. Each line is written as 04/03 0715 hrs 1.42 m PT, being date, time, upstream level and keeper's initials in that order. Nothing is erased; a wrong line is struck through once and rewritten below. The book is collected quarterly by the navigation clerk, who copies the levels into the district return and files the originals. Keepers who find the previous shift's entries incomplete should note the gap rather than fill it in from memory.

before:
Depot Standing Policy — Reckoning of Working Days

Several parts of this document count periods in working days: the seven days allowed for collecting held goods, the fourteen days for appealing a storage charge, and the three days of notice before a pallet is broken down. For the purposes of this scheme a working day means Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. Periods begin on the day after the notice is issued and end at the close of gate hours. Where a period would end on a day the scheme does not count, it ends on the next day that is counted. The gate clerk keeps the calendar from which all such reckonings are made.
after:
Depot Standing Policy — Reckoning of Working Days

Periods begin on the day after the notice is issued and end at the close of gate hours. Where a period would end on a day the scheme does not count, it ends on the next day that is counted. before:
Millpond Silt Survey — Report to the Trustees

The survey was carried out over three dry days in late September, with the hatches down and the leat drawn off. Probing on a two-metre grid gave a mean depth of accumulated silt of 340 millimetres across the pond, deepening towards the inflow. The silt trap at the head of the leat was found to be two-thirds full, and the grating above it was clear of debris. The stone apron below the wheel pit shows no new movement since the last inspection. Trustees are asked to consider whether desilting should be programmed for the coming winter or deferred a further year.
